deep.reconstruction:
Context. The previous page is headed 'Berechnung der Bahn der Vesta, aus den Örtern vom 29 März, 8 April, 18 April' (1807). It reduces the three observations and fixes the constants of the problem: the auxiliary angle σ = 14'47.30", log c = 3.2072964, log e = 9.7122097n, a = 0.93564565, b, d = -6.711512, and log λ, λ'', x, x''. This page carries out Gauss's 'method of hypotheses' for a first orbit from three geocentric places, in the form published in Theoria Motus (1809), Book II, Section I. The quantities are P = n''/n (ratio of the triangles between the radii) and Q = 2((n+n'')/n' - 1) r'^3. Two hypotheses are worked, and then the elements are derived.

(1) Erste Hypothese.
- Start values: log P = 0 and log Q = 8.4711628. This is the usual first guess P ≈ θ''/θ, Q ≈ θθ''.
- log Q + log c = 8.4711628 + 3.2072964. Further logarithmic terms (0.1868259, 0.7567511n, 9.5300748n, together with log e = 9.7122097n) combine into the auxiliary angle ω with log tan ω = 9.2422845, so ω = 9°54'33.77".
- The key equation is of the form c' sin ω sin^4 z = sin(z - ω - σ), solved for z by trial:
  - ω + σ = 9°54'33.77" + 14'47.30" = 10°9'21.07".
  - The correction is +33'45.59", giving z = 10°43'6.66".
  - Auxiliary logs: 1.6784592, 9.2357566 = log sin ω, 0.9142158, 7.0779036.
- log r' = log(R' sin δ') - log sin z = 9.6193432 - 9.2694759 = 0.3498673.
- Angles used later:
  - z - σ' = 10°28'19.36".
  - z - 4°55'34.91" = 5°47'31.75".
  - z - 4°41'37.47" = 6°1'29.19".
- Two parallel columns give r and r'' through the coefficients λ, λ'', x, x'' (0.5744448, 0.2383269, 0.6938855n, 0.7227741n). The results are log r = 0.3517852 and log r'' = 0.3479966.
- A block of sines and cosines gives the heliocentric angles between the radii. Their halves are 3°1'16.94" and 2°59'42.38"; the total heliocentric arc 2f' is 6°0'59.23", whose half is 3°0'29 248/402".
- Sector-to-triangle ratios (Theoria Motus art. 88 ff.):
  - Log differences: 0.3498673 - 0.3479966 = 0.0018707 and 0.3517852 - 0.3498673 = 0.0019179. Divided by 4: 0.0004676¾ and 0.0004794¾.
  - These define the auxiliary angle via tan(45°+ω) = (r'/r)^{1/4}. Here ω = 1'51 11/168" and 2ω = 3'42 11/84" (and 1'53 147/172", 3'47 61/86" for the other pair).
  - log sqrt(r r') = 0.3489319½ and 0.3508262½.
  - Adding 0.3008791 (≈ log 2cos of the half-angle) gives 0.6498110½ and 0.6517078½. Three times these gives 1.9494331½ and 1.9551235½.
  - log m = 2 log(kt) - 3 log(2 cos f · sqrt(r r')), giving 6.5217296½ and 6.5160194½.
  - The column '…1738.46 / 11.61 / 1750.07 / 8333333' is l + ξ + 5/6, with 5/6 = 0.8333333. It enters h = m/(5/6 + l + ξ), from which the ratio y (sector/triangle) is obtained: log values 0.0003847 and 0.0003796.
- Corrections to the start values: the terms -472, -3821, +5988, +2993 sum to +4688 (units of the 7th decimal). Hence the new values are l.P = 0.0000025 and l.Q = 8.4711628 + 0.0004688 = 8.4716316.

(2) Zweite Hypothese.
- P = 1.0000058 (reading uncertain), with the same a = 0.93564565 and d = -6.711512.
- Results: log tan ω = 9.2422862 and ω = 9°54'33.90".
- ω + σ = 10°9'21.20"; the correction is 33'48.40", so z = 10°43'9.60".
- log r' = 9.6193432 - 9.2695088 = 0.3498344.
- Angles: z - σ' = 10°28'22.31", 5°47'34.70", 6°1'32.14".
- log r = 0.3517504 and log r'' = 0.3479608. These same values are used on the next page.
- Half arcs: 3°1'18.48" + 2°59'43.88" = 6°1'2.36" = 2f', with half 3°0'31.18".
- The hypotheses have converged.

(3) Elements.
- Arguments of latitude u = 124°59'38.69" and u'' = 159°27'38.61", compared with y = 125°54'47.59" (the γ of the previous page) and y'' = 158°46'59.67".
  - (u+u'')/2 = 142°13'38.65" and (u''-u)/2 = 17°13'59.96".
  - (u+y)/2 = 125°27'13.14" and (y-u)/2 = 27'34.45".
  - (u''+y'')/2 = 159°7'19.14" and (y''-u'')/2 = -20'19.47".
- These half-sums and half-differences feed Gauss's (Napier-analogy type) spherical formulas, giving g = 86°5'0.40", h = 104°42'48.38", and half the inclination i/2 = 3°32'54 256/341". Hence i = 7°5'49.50".
- Node from two determinations, 103°8'54.17" and 103°8'52.59"; mean ☊ = 103°8'53.38".
- Longitudes in orbit, each a mean of two values: 183°12'50.64" and 189°13'53.00". Their difference is 6°1'2.36" = 2f', which checks the arc above.
- Semi-major axis: from 4·Δlog r, the series terms and 5/6 = 0.8333333333, Gauss gets log a = 0.3728428, i.e. a = 2.359624.
- Eccentricity angle: φ/2 = 2°47'52"-1/8, and φ = 5°35'43.89" (e = sin φ ≈ 0.0975; log e = 8.9890276 on the next page).
- The next page continues with the perihelion (249°7'58") and the constants for an ephemeris.
- All the elements are close to Vesta's actual orbit (a ≈ 2.36, i ≈ 7.1°, ☊ ≈ 103.9°, e ≈ 0.09).
errors: First hypothesis: the two half arcs 3°1'16.94" + 2°59'42.38" sum to 6°0'59.32", not the 6°0'59.23" (= 2×3°0'29 248/402") written. This is a 0.09" inconsistency, or else a misreading of one digit. In the second hypothesis the corresponding sum is exact (6°1'2.36").
Second hypothesis: z - σ' = 10°43'9.60" - 14'47.30" = 10°28'22.30"; the page has 22.31". This is a trivial rounding difference of 0.01".

results.what: Determination of a planetary orbit from three geocentric observations by successive hypotheses on P = n''/n and Q, solving c sin ω sin^4 z = sin(z-ω-σ) for the Earth-angle z and hence r'
results.modern_name: Gauss's method of initial orbit determination (Gauss method, method of hypotheses)
results.usually_credited_to: C. F. Gauss, Theoria Motus 1809 (first used for Ceres 1801)

results.what: Ratio of sector to triangle via tan(45°+ω) = (r'/r)^{1/4}, l, m and h = m/(5/6 + l + ξ)
results.modern_name: Gauss's sector-to-triangle ratio (Gauss's equations for y)

results.usually_credited_to: Gauss 1807 (his rapid Vesta orbit is historically documented)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of Gauss's well-documented 1807 first orbit of Vesta, using exactly the method later published in Theoria Motus. It is valuable as a record of the numerical workflow (two hypotheses, convergence), but it contains nothing not already credited to him.
